approachQuestion.prompt:
Choosing valuable maintenance jobs

Each proposed job has a half-open required machine interval [start,end) and a positive integer value. Choose non-overlapping jobs to maximize total value; jobs touching at an endpoint are compatible. Return only the maximum value, with 0 allowed for no jobs. The unsorted job array is immutable.

Input: jobs=[(0,3,4),(3,6,4),(0,6,10),(6,8,3)]
Output: 13
Choose (0,6,10) and (6,8,3).

Input: jobs=[(1,2,3),(2,4,5),(1,4,7)]
Output: 8

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000000000; 1 ≤ value ≤ 1000000; totals fit signed 64-bit arithmetic. Use comparison-based ordering and searches. Choose the best worst-case running time among the listed methods.

options.text: Sort copied jobs by end. For each job i, binary-search earlier jobs for the last end at most its start. Set the best value for the first i jobs to the larger of skipping i or taking its value plus the best prefix ending at that compatible predecessor.
options.feedback: Every optimal selection either omits the current job or includes it. In the second case, all other chosen jobs lie in the compatible prefix, so the transition considers every possible optimal selection.

options.text: Sort by end and greedily keep each compatible job, adding its value.
options.feedback: For [(0,3,4),(3,6,4),(0,6,10)], the greedy rule obtains 8 but the long job alone is worth 10. Maximizing count does not maximize unequal values.

options.text: Process jobs in decreasing value and keep a job if it conflicts with none already chosen.
options.feedback: For [(0,6,10),(0,3,6),(3,6,6)], taking value 10 first blocks a compatible pair worth 12. The greatest individual value is not a safe local choice.

options.text: Sort by end and use the same include-or-skip prefix recurrence, but find each compatible predecessor by scanning backward through earlier jobs.
options.feedback: The recurrence is correct and recognizes the needed weighted prefix state. But repeated predecessor scans can be replaced with binary searches because the ends are ordered.

feedback.reason: Replace an invalid unweighted greedy rule with weighted include-or-skip state and compatible-prefix lookup.
details: Copy jobs and sort by end using iterative bottom-up merge sort and a reusable buffer. Allocate n+1 best-value cells. For each job, use iterative binary search over earlier ends and fill one DP cell from the include-or-skip recurrence. Keep no chosen-job reconstruction.

At each end-sorted job, compare skipping it with taking its value plus the best compatible predecessor state. A locally highest-value job may block a more valuable combination; this is a weighted recurrence, not unweighted earliest-finish selection.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For weighted-prefix-dp, n is the number of jobs. Include sorting, all predecessor searches and DP construction. Count copied jobs, buffer and DP array. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Sorting and n predecessor searches dominate linear DP transitions.
details: Sorting costs O(n log n). There are n predecessor searches, each logarithmic, and n constant-time DP transitions. Copies, reusable sorting buffer and DP array all require O(n) auxiliary space. The analyzed implementation is iterative, so no recursive search stack is present.
Comparison merge sort, iterative predecessor binary searches and bottom-up DP; scalar result.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(n)”: Linear backward predecessor search is a different variant. The analyzed method uses logarithmic binary searches.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The copied jobs, sort buffer and n+1 DP cells all count as linear auxiliary storage.
“Time O(2^n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The include-or-skip recurrence is evaluated once per job in a table. It does not recursively enumerate all subsets.
